commitsOnCulpritFiles.title: fix(content-manager): deduplicate MCP tool names when an api has multiple content types
commitsOnCulpritFiles.effect: Landed in the MCP area but touched only packages/core/content-manager/server/src/mcp/utils.ts, its test file and docs/docs/docs/01-core/strapi/mcp-server.md; the ACTIONS map and the tool auth policies are untouched, so it does not affect this finding.

source.howDecided: git log c43e9ee1e2..origin/develop -- packages/core/content-manager/server/src/services/permission-checker.ts packages/core/content-manager/server/src/mcp/derive-content-type-mcp-tools.ts returns zero commits. Read both files at today's head: permission-checker.ts lines 6-14 still map publish and unpublish to 'plugin::content-manager.explorer.publish' (lines 11-12) and discard to 'plugin::content-manager.explorer.update' (line 13). derive-content-type-mcp-tools.ts still attaches auth: { policies: [{ action: ACTIONS.discard, subject: uid }] } at line 296 (collection types) and line 504 (single types), against ACTIONS.publish at 278/486 and ACTIONS.unpublish at 287/495. The one MCP commit in the range (#27357) is a tool-name dedup in mcp/utils.ts and does not touch the permission mapping. The code is correct and unchanged; the wrong text is entirely on the docs side.

docs.note: git log c768c7bf..origin/main -- docusaurus/docs/cms/features/strapi-mcp-server.md is empty. Both wrong cells are still there, at the same line numbers the review recorded: line 233 (collection types) and line 244 (single types), each reading '| `discard_draft` | Discard draft | `publish` | Discard draft changes and revert to the published version |'. Second permalink for the single-type row: https://github.com/strapi/documentation/blob/9226f90506a4a361038f220f24768016a73b5663/docusaurus/docs/cms/features/strapi-mcp-server.md#L244 . The correct value is `update` in both rows. Also still true at line 232: '| `unpublish` | Unpublish | `publish` |', which is right only because ACTIONS.unpublish is literally the same string as ACTIONS.publish.

citedItems.note: The PR that created the page with the wrong permission cell already in it. Origin, not a fix. Unchanged.
Introduced the MCP server and wired discard_<slug>_draft to ACTIONS.discard. Correct behavior, cited only to identify the code the doc misdescribes. Unchanged.

reevaluation: The finding stands exactly as written. Neither side moved: the ACTIONS map and the MCP tool auth policies are unchanged on develop through v5.52.1, and both wrong table cells are verbatim on strapi/documentation main at lines 233 and 244. Every claim in the review's fixedAfter block re-verifies. The one new piece of context is strapi/strapi#27395 (opened 2026-08-17), a separate MCP defect about the advertised JSON Schema dialect; it confirms the MCP surface is getting outside scrutiny right now but has no bearing on this finding's verdict, confidence or scope. Verdict remains doc-bug, confidence high, scope two cells in one file.
policyBasis: strapi/documentation .github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/config.yml: 'blank_issues_enabled: false' with the only contact link being 'Strapi Project Issues ... Please use the strapi/strapi repo for these issues', so a wrong sentence in the docs is filed in strapi/documentation via .github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/BUG_REPORT.yml ('Documentation Bug Report', title prefix '[Bug]: ', label 'type: bug'), whose required fields are 'Link to the documentation page or resource' and 'Describe the bug', with optional 'Suggested improvements or fixes' and 'Related issue(s)/PR(s)'.
notes: A fix must touch BOTH rows (233 collection types, 244 single types); patching only the first leaves the single-type table wrong. The correct cell value is `update`, corroborated by three independent code paths: the MCP tool policy (derive-content-type-mcp-tools.ts:296/504 -> ACTIONS.discard), the admin REST route policy for discard, and the admin UI Discard button gated on canUpdate. Worth mentioning in the same issue that `unpublish` has no permission of its own (ACTIONS.unpublish === ACTIONS.publish), so `publish` always grants both tools. The BUG_REPORT template's 'Related issue(s)/PR(s)' field should cite strapi/documentation#3194 as the origin of the cell.
